subject: Deployment boundary definitions for Dedicated/Private - architecture and evidence

Subject: Request: network boundaries + evidence for SOC 2/SIG/CAIQ review

Jonas,

We're preparing our vendor SIG assessment packet and need a concise explanation of how Redwood separates customer data, the management/control plane, and operator access for your Dedicated and Private deployment options. Specifically we need:

- A one-page diagram showing the customer data path vs management path for both Dedicated and Private deployments (VPC peering, private link, or on-prem VPN options)
- Statement on how operator/admin access is constrained (bastion, ephemeral credentials, MFA, jump hosts)
- Evidence pointers for SIG/SOC2: flow logs, KMS key usage, rotation cadence, audit log retention windows, and any separation-of-duties controls

Can you send those plus any supporting artifacts (diagram PNG/PDF and a zipped evidence index) by EOD Friday? Happy to accept redacted artifacts.

Thanks,
Lisa

Attached: deployment-boundary-diagram-v1.png

High level notes to pair with the diagram (short bullets we can paste into the questionnaire):

- Customer data plane: For Hosted/Dedicated we either terminate customer traffic in a tenant-dedicated GPU pool (Dedicated) or in a Redwood shared tenancy with strict logical separation (Hosted). For Private deployments we support VPC peering (AWS TGW) or customer-managed VPN/Direct Connect to keep egress into customer-controlled networks.

- Management plane separation: Control plane (model registry, orchestration) is a logically separate cluster and uses private control endpoints. Operator/admin access to control plane is restricted to a separate mgmt network that is never NAT'd into customer data subnets. All management traffic is mutual-TLS with client certs + enforced mTLS for internal service-to-service.

- Operator access: SSO enforced (SAML/OIDC) with MFA. For Dedicated/Private, operator session work is done from ephemeral bastion hosts with ephemeral certs issued via our internal CA. Least-privilege IAM roles with just-in-time elevation used for troubleshooting; sessions are captured (session recording) and forward-ported to audit logs.

- Encryption: TLS1.2+ (prefer TLS1.3 where available) in transit; AES-256 at rest. Customer keys are supported via customer-managed KMS in Private deployments (BYOK option). Key rotation policy: monthly automated key rotation for service keys; customer-managed keys follow customer's KMS cadence.

- Logging & evidence: VPC flow logs (or equivalent packet-level summaries) retained 90 days by default; audit trails (API, admin actions) retained 2 years for SOC2 evidence. For SIG: we can provide anonymized VPC flow samples, KMS access logs, and screenshots of audit entries. Network evidence bundle prepared as a sanitized zip.

I kept this intentionally terse for the questionnaire. If they want deeper network ACL/SG rules we can add a redacted snippet.

Marissa Cole
Principal Infra Architect
Redwood Inference

Attachment: deployment-boundary-diagram-v1.png (1.2MB) - one-page diagram showing: customer ingress -> customer subnet -> dedicated GPU pool (tenant tag) OR private runtime in customer VPC -> control plane endpoints (private) -> operator bastion path (SSO + ephemeral certs)

Quick ops notes for the reply to Acme:

- On-prem / air-gapped option: we provide an on-prem package where the control plane is deployed into a customer-controlled management cluster; network connectivity is one-way for telemetry collection (pull model) and admin sessions are proxied via customer-managed bastions. We will state that in writing and include a short checklist of isolation controls available in the on-prem package.
- Bastion ops: ephemeral images rebuilt daily, cert rotation every 24 hours for ephemeral sessions, and we automate key revocation through our internal CA.
- Redaction guidance: remove CIDR blocks and customer hostnames from any flow samples; use synthetic IPs or prefixes.

I'll assemble the small ops checklist and include an example bastion session record (redacted) in the ZIP.

Hi Lisa — thanks for the clear asks. Attached are two artifacts for your reviewer: 1) deployment-boundary-diagram-v1.png (one-page diagram as requested) and 2) network-evidence-bundle-2026-02-13.zip (sanitized samples and an index).

Summary (paste-ready):
- We separate the customer data plane from the management/control plane via logically distinct VPCs and private endpoints. Dedicated deployments run in tenant-tagged, isolated runtime pools; Private deployments can use VPC peering or customer-managed VPN/Direct Connect to keep traffic inside customer networks.
- Operator/admin access requires SSO + MFA and occurs only through ephemeral bastion hosts with just-in-time elevation; sessions are recorded and logged.
- All service-to-service communication uses mutual TLS. Data in transit is TLS; at rest uses AES-256. For Private we support BYOK with customer-managed KMS.
- Evidence included: redacted VPC flow sample, KMS access log sample, API audit entries, bastion session index, and the one-page diagram. Retention: flow logs 90 days; audit trails 2 years (SOC2 evidence).

If this looks good we'll send a short cover email linking each artifact to the SIG/SOC2 control IDs and offer a 30-minute walkthrough with our security engineer (Karthik). Please let me know if Acme needs any additional redactions or a PDF diagram instead of PNG.

Best,
Jonas Weber
